title: SET_CONFIGURATION with a configuration_index that does not exist: answer NO_SUCH_DESCRIPTOR
body:
SET_CONFIGURATION with a configuration_index that has no CONFIGURATION descriptor (for example 1 on a single-configuration entity) is answered BAD_ARGUMENTS today, carrying the current index. The E_SCFG CHECK_ARG against configurations_count branches to E_SCFGBAD, and testbench item A3 asserts BAD_ARGUMENTS.

Owner decision 2026-10-17: answer **NO_SUCH_DESCRIPTOR**.

Specification trace, from the local IEEE 1722.1-2021 and Milan v1.2 Consolidated (2023-11-30) texts:
- IEEE 1722.1-2021 7.4.7.1: configuration_index "is set to descriptor_index of the new configuration". The response always carries the current value: the old one when the command fails.
- IEEE 1722.1-2021 7.4.7.2 (restrictions) names only STREAM_IS_RUNNING, ENTITY_LOCKED/ENTITY_ACQUIRED and NOT_AUTHENTICATED. It sets no status for an index that does not exist.
- IEEE 1722.1-2021 Table 7-141: NO_SUCH_DESCRIPTOR (2) means no descriptor exists with the given descriptor_type and descriptor_index; BAD_ARGUMENTS (7) means one or more field values are bad. A missing CONFIGURATION descriptor matches NO_SUCH_DESCRIPTOR more precisely.
- Milan v1.2 5.4.2.5: implement per [ATDECC 7.4.7], adding STREAM_IS_RUNNING while bound or streaming and the lock rule. Nothing on the index.
- Unchanged: a bound or streaming entity still answers STREAM_IS_RUNNING first (Milan v1.2 5.4.2.5).

Done when:
- an out-of-range configuration_index answers NO_SUCH_DESCRIPTOR with the current index;
- STREAM_IS_RUNNING keeps its precedence;
- testbench item A3 is updated to the new status, with a planted mutant;
- the decision is recorded in the compliance review with the clauses above;
- the processor suites and the parent consumer gates pass.

Out of scope, to be reported only: whether READ_DESCRIPTOR answers the same way for a missing CONFIGURATION index.
